The turkey is the line item that jumped this year.

Feeding 10 on Thursday runs $58.63 — about $5.86 a plate — up 6% from $55.18 last year and the first rise since 2022, after three straight years of falling prices (American Farm Bureau Federation, 41st annual survey, prices checked early November).

The 16-lb frozen turkey leads it: $23.68, up $2.38 or 10%. Cranberries are up about 9%, dinner rolls 7%, sweet potatoes 5%. A few things fell — the veggie tray and pie ingredients — but the bird set the tone.

It's still roughly 8% below the 2022 record of $64.05, and stores are discounting hard: some shoppers found turkey as low as 69 cents a pound.

My take: this is a shop-the-deals year, not a skip-the-bird year — the loss-leader turkey is the one thing worth chasing a sale on.
